report.title: Harness Internals: the home directory you never look at
report.subject: What Claude Code and OpenAI Codex CLI write into their home directories, and which of it is undocumented
report.evidence_boundary: One macOS machine (Darwin 24.3.0, Apple silicon) measured on 2026-08-11 under heavy daily use of both tools, plus vendor documentation, vendor issue trackers, and published security research. Structure was recorded; file contents, credentials, and message text were not.

evidence_labels.MEASURED: Read directly off the sampled machine on 2026-08-11
evidence_labels.REPORTED: Published by a third party; treated as weaker evidence

disk_breakdown.note: single orphaned checkout; git worktree prune cannot reclaim
plugin sync scratch not cleaned after success

file_classes.name: Complete record of your work
file_classes.contains: Every prompt, model reply, tool call, and full tool result, as plain text
file_classes.why_it_matters: Any secret the agent ever read is stored here in plain text. .gitignore has no effect.

file_classes.name: Shadow copies of your source code
file_classes.contains: Pre-edit file versions, oversized tool output, entire additional git checkouts
file_classes.why_it_matters: A repository you deleted is not gone if a worktree copy survives.

file_classes.name: Fingerprints of you and your machine
file_classes.contains: Shell functions, PATH, every trusted directory path, git remotes, machine ID, prompt history
file_classes.why_it_matters: The trust list is a permanent dated record of every directory you have worked in.

file_classes.name: Credentials
file_classes.why_it_matters: 0600 stops other users, not malware running as you. Actively targeted by the ChainDrop worm.

file_classes.name: State the vendor pushes to you
file_classes.contains: 487 cached feature flags, server-side restrictions, compliance taints, monitoring notice
file_classes.why_it_matters: Disabling telemetry also disables the remote kill-switch channel.

file_classes.name: Telemetry queued on disk
file_classes.contains: Platform, Node version, terminal, model, session id, entry point. No prompt text in sample.
file_classes.why_it_matters: Codex exports tool results even when log_user_prompt is off, and tool results contain file contents.

file_classes.name: Leftovers
file_classes.why_it_matters: About 1.08 GB, 27% of total, is pure reclaimable waste.

file_classes.name: Things that can execute
file_classes.contains: Shell commands run automatically, downloaded plugin bundles, a full macOS app
file_classes.why_it_matters: A hook committed to a repository runs when you start a session in it.

codex-cli.note: session_meta.base_instructions stores the full system prompt in every one of the 453 rollout files

risks.name: .gitignore does not stop secrets reaching disk
risks.mechanism: gitignore controls commits, not reads. Agent reads file, output lands in toolUseResult, transcript persists.
risks.fix: Keep real secrets out of reachable files; use permissions deny rules; rotate anything already seen.

risks.name: A cloned repository can run code at session start
risks.mechanism: Project .claude/settings.json can define a SessionStart hook. ChainDrop worm used this across 400+ npm packages.
risks.fix: Inspect .claude/, .codex/, .vscode/ before opening an unfamiliar repository with an agent.

risks.name: Agent state gets committed to a shared repository
risks.mechanism: No .gitignore across 12 sampled repositories mentioned .claude at all.
risks.fix: Global gitignore for settings.local.json and session-env; keep skills and rules committed.

risks.name: Directory layout is a permanent readable list
risks.mechanism: Trust lists, project keys, and git_origin_url are never pruned, including for paths that no longer exist.
risks.fix: No supported prune command exists; edit config.toml and ~/.claude/projects by hand.

risks.name: Telemetry, and the trap in switching it off
risks.mechanism: DISABLE_TELEMETRY also stops feature flag fetching, which carries remote kill switches.
risks.fix: Choose a posture deliberately; the middle position keeps the safety channel.

traps.reads_as: 0 means never clean up, keep forever
traps.actually_does: 0 stops transcripts being written to disk at all
Also stops feature flag fetching, so remote kill switches stop arriving
traps.correct_usage: Accept the trade knowingly, or use the middle posture

traps.actually_does: Caps the prompt history file only, not sessions/, which held 1.37 GB
A request to a model, not an enforced boundary; secrets have still been read
traps.correct_usage: Use permissions deny rules, which the harness enforces

traps.actually_does: Also deletes that project's agent memory at memory/MEMORY.md

limits: One machine, one operating system, one point in time. Numbers prove a file class exists; they do not establish typical size.
macOS only. Credential storage differs on Linux, which changes the risk picture.
Heavy usage skews absolute sizes upward. Proportions transfer better than absolutes.
No network capture was performed. Claims about transmission come from documentation and locally queued telemetry only.
Undocumented is a claim about documentation coverage, not about intent. Every file examined had an obvious engineering purpose.
Some Codex directories were identified by name and size only, such as pets/ and visualizations/, which were empty or nearly empty.
